name: infra_dvc_stages
title: A DVC pipeline: params.yaml + dvc.yaml + three `python -m src.stages.<name>` entrypoints, with the temporal split in the second one
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: the config-and-stages repo shape, with the time signal one file away from the split
note: Two planted defects, one recovered. MLV602 fires. MLV106 does NOT, and the reason is the project shape: every temporal signal the rule looks for lives in `prepare.py` (`parse_dates=[date_column]` at line 27, `.sort_values(date_column)` at line 28, a DatetimeIndex and a `.resample()` at line 59, and lag/rolling features built off the target) while the `train_test_split(..., shuffle=True)` lives in `train.py`. Splitting a pipeline into DVC stages is the whole point of DVC, and MLV106 reads its signals per module. See the domain-infra round-2 report, finding INFRA-R2-13. The MLV602 that does fire carries a false evidence row - `a global seed is set elsewhere in the workspace, which does make this split reproducible` - and is de-rated 0.950 -> 0.617 on the strength of it; the only seeding in this project is `random_state=seed` on the HistGradientBoostingRegressor at line 37, which does nothing for train_test_split. See INFRA-R2-14. Two `config_unresolved` diagnostics correctly say MLView did not open params.yaml, which is the documented deferral and exactly the right thing to say.
stagesObserved: config, data, model, train, eval and deliver present; preprocess and objective absent, which is correct for a gradient-boosting regressor with no explicit transformer or loss object. `--relevance ml` and `--relevance all` are identical (5 files either way).

expected.defect: train_test_split(..., shuffle=True) on a chronologically sorted, lag-featured demand table
expected.why: every feature in this table is a lag or a rolling mean of the target, so a random cut lets the model interpolate hour t from hours t-1 and t+1; the reported MAE is not the error it would make on the future, which is the only error that matters for a demand model
`dvc repro` exists to make a stage reproducible; with an unseeded split the metrics file this pipeline tracks changes on every run and cannot be compared with its own history

forbidden.why: nothing is fitted in the prepare stage: shift(), rolling().mean() and resample() are not fitted transforms and there is no splitter in this file
the only fit in this stage is model.fit(x_train, y_train) at line 56, an estimator fit on the training partition, after the split at line 52
x_hold never reaches a fit; it is written to parquet and read back by the evaluate stage
there is no cross-validation call in this project
mae, rmse and mape are regression metrics and they are fed model.predict(...), a continuous prediction, which is what they take
there is no ranking metric in this file; roc_auc_score and average_precision_score do not appear

base.seed in params.yaml reaches the estimator as random_state=seed at line 37, so a random_state= keyword does exist in the workspace. The split's own missing random_state is MLV602's finding and it is labelled expected above
there is no splitter in the prepare stage
this is joblib.dump of an sklearn estimator, not torch.save, and nothing in the project calls torch.load
